New Music Friday: Fontaines D.C., The Avalanches and the Albums Worth Your Attention This Week

Curated & written by Kabir Mehta

If you only have time to listen to a handful of albums this month, Friday, October 16 is the day to pick them. It is one of the busiest release days of the autumn, with guitar bands, producers, singer-songwriters and a few veterans all arriving at once. Here is a guide to the records people are talking about, along with a few from last week that deserve a second look.

The Headliners

Fontaines D.C. are back with Dopamine Chamber on XL Recordings, and reviewers are calling it the band's most experimental and daring record so far. AllMusic named it an Editors' Choice, and NPR Music put it first on its list of the week's best. If you know the Irish group only as a guitar band, this one will probably surprise you in the best way.

The Avalanches return with No Bad Memories on Modular. The Australian collective has built its reputation on sample-based music that feels like a dream assembled from old records, and this release continues that tradition. The anonymous artist known as @ delivers Autosmile on 4AD, a genre-blending record that critics have praised for pushing experimental pop forward. Two more picks from NPR's list are Sophia Stel's The Greatest Album of All Time on A24 Music and June McDoom's Follow the Light on Jagjaguwar.

Singer-Songwriters and Pop

Rachel Chinouriri, the Croydon-born singer-songwriter, releases her second album, I think I spoke too soon, and it finds her leaning into vulnerability. Ashe returns with The Girl of Your Dreams, and Angèle, the Belgian star, delivers Instinct. Elsewhere, Florrie is out with Magic for a While, Grace Carter has When Saturn Returns, and Andy Grammer adds Big Stupid Heart to the pile. R&B fans have Lucky Daye's Aloud! and Nao's Autumn to explore.

Hip-Hop, Soul and Beyond

UK rap veteran Tinie Tempah is back with The Night's Not Dead, his first project in nine years, and it will be fascinating to see how longtime fans respond. Gotts Street Park, a Leeds trio, blend modern soul, jazz and hip-hop on their second album, Somewhere Between. Lucki has also put out a new tape, Last Laugh, as part of an archive release, and Pi'erre Bourne has issued a deluxe edition of Made in Paris.

The Quieter Corners

Some of the most interesting releases are the ones that will never trend. Max Richter has released While the Flood Rages with the choir Tenebrae, and Brian Eno has put out Another Day on Earth. Folk and Americana fans have Richard Thompson's Hippies, Thugs and Heroes on New West, and Eivør's Tungl is out on Nuclear Blast. Metal listeners can try Insomnium's Netherworlds. And if you enjoy nostalgia, Andy Shauf's The Party has received a tenth-anniversary expansion with nine bonus tracks, including previously unreleased material.

Last Week's Highlights

The week before was no slouch either. October 9 brought new records from Cameron Winter, Troye Sivan and Remi Wolf, along with Tinashe's Popstar and Sheryl Crow's Pick You Up. Fatima Al Qadiri's 3TWI on Hyperdub also arrived that day, along with albums from Bodega and Jeremiah Chu. If you missed any of those, this weekend is a good time to catch up.

How to Listen Without Getting Overwhelmed

This much new music can feel like homework, so here is a simple approach. Pick one album from outside your usual taste, one from an artist you already love, and one wildcard from the quieter corners. Give each a full, uninterrupted listen, ideally with headphones and no scrolling. Albums reveal themselves slowly, and the ones that sound strange on the first play are often the ones that stay with you.

Next week is no quieter. Anderson .Paak and Cordae, Michael Kiwanuka, John Legend and others arrive on October 23, so there will be plenty more to explore very soon.
